questions.question: What was the main persistent-emission result from the Fermi/LAT search of 4U 0142+61?

options.A: No significant detection; the authors reported upper limits in two GeV bands
options.B: A steady source was detected above 10 GeV
options.C: A strong pulsed signal was found in both bands
options.D: A 4σ detection established a spectral cutoff at 230 keV

questions.rationale: The LAT analysis found no significant persistent source and used flux limits to constrain models.
questions.evidence_quote: which result in no signiﬁcant detection

questions.question: What likelihood result did the 15° region fit yield, and what did that imply?

options.A: TS≈0.23, corresponding to less than 1σ significance
options.C: TS≈59.6, indicating a highly significant gamma-ray source
options.D: TS≈0, proving the source emits no photons

questions.rationale: The broad-region fit gave a very low TS value, below 1σ.
questions.evidence_quote: The ﬁt yields a Test Statistics (TS) value of ∼0.23

questions.question: Why did the authors also perform spectral analysis using a 2° region around the source?

options.A: To avoid contamination from nearby bright sources
options.B: To improve the RXTE pulse timing baseline
options.C: To remove the Galactic diffuse model entirely
options.D: To isolate only photons above 10 GeV

questions.rationale: The smaller ROI was chosen for spectral analysis to reduce nearby-source contamination.
questions.evidence_quote: in order to completely avoid contamination from the nearby bright sources

questions.question: What photon data and exposure formed the principal LAT dataset?

options.A: Data from 2008 Aug 4 to 2010 Apr 29 within 15° and about 31.7 Ms exposure
options.B: Data from 2004 to 2008 within 2° and 196 ks exposure
options.C: Data from one month in 2010 within 40° and 3.17 Ms
options.D: Data from 2008 Aug 4 to 2010 Apr 30 with 15 ks exposure

questions.rationale: The paper states the selected LAT collection interval and exposure.
questions.evidence_quote: collected from 2008 August 4 to 2010 April 29 with an exposure time of ∼31.7 Ms.

questions.question: How was the RXTE spin ephemeris derived from the PCA observations?

options.A: Cross-correlate grouped pulse profiles with a template and fit phase shifts with a polynomial
options.B: Use a Fourier transform of the LAT photons alone
options.C: Fit a single sinusoid to unbarycentered HEXTE data
options.D: Average 53 independent period estimates without phase connection

questions.rationale: They generated a template, cross-correlated grouped pointings, then fit phase shifts.

questions.question: What polynomial order best fit the RXTE phase shifts over the LAT observing span?
questions.rationale: The paper identifies a cubic polynomial as the best-fitting model.

questions.question: What were the 3σ RMS pulsed-fraction limits in the 0.2–1.0 and 1.0–10.0 GeV bands?
questions.rationale: The lower and higher GeV bands have those RMS pulse-fraction limits.
questions.evidence_quote: a 3σ upper limit to the RMS pulsed fraction of 1.5% in the 0.2−1.0 GeV band and 2.3% in the 1.0−10.0 GeV band.

questions.question: What upper limit did the authors infer for the spectral break energy by connecting the two LAT flux limits?
questions.rationale: The extrapolated curves intersect around 1.1 MeV, giving an upper limit to the break.
questions.evidence_quote: at ∼1.1 MeV which is an upper limit to the spectral break energy

questions.question: How did the paper qualify its constraint on the QED model if the optical excess is intrinsic to the neutron star?

options.A: The lack of a 10–200 MeV rise constrains the model, but not stringently
options.B: The LAT data definitively exclude the model at all energies
options.C: The optical excess proves a continuous MeV rise
options.D: The model predicts no emission below 1 GeV, so the result is irrelevant

questions.rationale: The authors state the constraint depends on the optical-excess origin and is not stringent.
questions.evidence_quote: our results place constraint, although not stringent, on the quantum electrodynamics model

questions.question: What physical process in the proposed magnetar-corona interpretation could suppress emission above roughly 1 MeV?

options.A: Photon splitting or electron–positron pair creation in the ultrastrong magnetic field
options.B: Inverse Compton scattering on Galactic diffuse photons
options.D: Cyclotron emission from the LAT tracker

questions.rationale: The cited model predicts photons above this range are trapped and split or create pairs.
questions.evidence_quote: photons with energies in excess of ≳1 MeV would be trapped in the ultrastrong magnetic ﬁelds
